players.product: Regulated electric service to data-center customers under electric service agreements (ESAs) with minimum take provisions

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's Q2 2026 10-Q (MD&A segment table): Electric Utilities and Infrastructure operating revenues were $7,175 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026 versus $7,045 million a year earlier, and $15,053 million in the six months versus $14,185 million; segment GWh sales were 64,442 versus 64,161 in the quarter, and net proportional MW capacity in operation was 55,820 versus 55,216.
quarterly_data.figure: EU&I operating revenues $7,175 million (Q2 2026) vs $7,045 million; 64,442 GWh; 55,820 MW in operation

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's Q2 2026 10-Q: capital expenditures were $8,240 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026 versus $6,428 million a year earlier (Electric Utilities and Infrastructure segment $7,463 million versus $5,724 million); the 10-Q says the investing-cash variance was primarily driven by proceeds from the sale of Piedmont's Tennessee business, partially offset by higher capital expenditures within the Electric Utilities and Infrastructure segment.
quarterly_data.figure: capital expenditures $8,240 million (six months ended June 30, 2026) vs $6,428 million; EU&I segment $7,463 million

quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy's Q2 2026 10-Q on the Person County combined-cycle units (Roxboro Plant, including the second 1,360-MW hydrogen-capable unit): Duke Energy Progress and NCEMC executed the contractual agreements for both units in April 2026, allowing NCEMC to own approximately 225 MW of each unit, for a total of approximately 450 MW; the joint ownership agreement was finalized and executed in June 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: NCEMC approximately 225 MW of each unit, approximately 450 MW in total
